questions.question: Which HTML5 element is used to specify a footer for a document or section?
questions.explanation: The <footer> tag defines a footer for a document or section, typically containing author, copyright, or contact info.

questions.question: What is the correct HTML5 Doctype declaration?
questions.explanation: In HTML5, the doctype is simplified to standard <!DOCTYPE html>.

questions.question: Which HTML attribute specifies an alternate text for an image if the image cannot be displayed?
questions.explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides alternate text for screen readers and in case the image fails to render.

questions.question: Which input type defines a slider control in HTML5 forms?
questions.explanation: <input type='range'> renders a slider control.

questions.question: Which tag is used to embed vector graphics directly into an HTML document?
questions.explanation: <svg> defines Scalable Vector Graphics directly in HTML markup.

questions.question: In CSS Flexbox, which property aligns items along the cross axis?
questions.explanation: align-items specifies the default alignment for items along the cross axis of the current flex line.

questions.question: What does 'box-sizing: border-box;' do to an element's calculation?
options: Includes padding and border within the element's specified width and height
questions.explanation: 'border-box' ensures padding and border are included inside width and height calculations.

questions.question: Which CSS Grid property defines the number and widths of columns in a grid layout?
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid columns.

questions.question: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: ID selectors (#main-header) have higher specificity (0,1,0,0) than classes or element tags.

questions.question: How do you apply styles only to screens narrower than 768px?
questions.explanation: @media (max-width: 768px) targets viewports from 0px up to 768px wide.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between 'let' and 'var' in JavaScript?
options: There is no difference in ES6
questions.explanation: 'let' has block scope ({ ... }), while 'var' is scoped to the enclosing function.

questions.question: What does the following code return: typeof NaN?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, NaN (Not-a-Number) is technically of the primitive type 'number'.

questions.question: What is a Closure in JavaScript?
options: A function that closes the browser window
A function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical environment
A private JSON object with no getters
A method for terminating asynchronous promises
questions.explanation: A closure gives an inner function access to its outer function's scope even after the outer function has returned.

questions.question: Which method creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function on every element?
questions.explanation: Array.prototype.map() returns a new transformed array without modifying the original.

questions.question: What is the result of '2' + 2 - 1 in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: '2' + 2 performs string concatenation -> '22'. Then '22' - 1 coerces to number -> 21.

questions.question: Which hook is used to perform side effects in functional React components?
questions.explanation: useEffect serves the purpose of lifecycle methods like componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, and componentWillUnmount.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of React's Virtual DOM?
options: It minimizes costly direct DOM re-renders by batching and computing minimal diffs
It stores state directly in the browser's database
questions.explanation: Virtual DOM reconciliation calculates the minimal set of real DOM operations necessary to reflect UI changes.

questions.question: In React, how do you pass data from a parent component down to a child component?
questions.explanation: Props (short for properties) are the standard unidirectional mechanism to pass data down the component hierarchy.

questions.question: Which hook memoizes expensive calculation results to prevent unnecessary recalculations on re-renders?
questions.explanation: useMemo caches the computed result of a function and only recalculates it when dependencies change.

questions.question: Why should keys be provided when rendering a list of elements in React?
options: Keys make elements visible to search engines
Keys help React identify which items have changed, been added, or removed for efficient updates
Keys allow CSS animations to run faster
questions.explanation: Unique keys give list items a persistent identity so React reconciles lists efficiently without re-rendering all nodes.

questions.question: Which component powers the asynchronous, non-blocking I/O event loop in Node.js?
questions.explanation: Libuv is the multi-platform C library that handles the event loop and asynchronous thread pool in Node.js.

questions.question: Which core Node.js module is used to read and write files synchronously or asynchronously?
questions.explanation: The 'fs' (file system) module provides both callback and promise-based APIs to interact with the file system.

questions.question: What does the 'npm' command stand for?
questions.explanation: NPM is the default package manager for Node.js.

questions.question: What is a Buffer in Node.js used for?
options: To handle raw binary data directly in memory
To speed up browser network requests
questions.explanation: The Buffer class provides instances to store and manipulate raw binary streams outside the V8 heap.

questions.question: How can you run multiple instances of Node.js that can distribute workloads across multi-core systems?
questions.explanation: The cluster module allows easy creation of child worker processes that all share server ports.

questions.question: What parameter in an Express middleware function is invoked to pass control to the next handler?
questions.explanation: Calling next() passes control to the subsequent middleware function in the request-response stack.

questions.question: Which built-in Express middleware is used to parse incoming requests with JSON payloads?
questions.explanation: express.json() is a built-in middleware function based on body-parser to parse application/json payloads.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code should be returned when a new resource is successfully created?
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 indicates that the request succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource.

questions.question: How do you access URL route parameters like '/students/:id' in Express?
questions.explanation: Named route parameters are captured and populated in the req.params object.

questions.question: How do you define an Express error-handling middleware function?
questions.explanation: Express identifies error-handling middleware by its 4-argument signature: (err, req, res, next).

questions.question: What binary format does MongoDB use internally to store and transmit documents?
questions.explanation: MongoDB stores data in BSON (Binary JSON), extending JSON with additional data types like Date and raw binary.

questions.question: Which operator is used to filter documents where a field matches any value in a specified array?
questions.explanation: The $in operator selects documents where the field's value matches any value in the provided array.

questions.question: In Mongoose, how do you define a foreign reference to another model?
questions.explanation: Mongoose references another collection using ObjectId and the 'ref' property for populate queries.

questions.question: What is an Aggregation Pipeline in MongoDB?
options: A tool for backing up collections
A multi-stage framework for data transformation, grouping, and statistical calculations
A plugin for exporting collections to CSV
A command to repair corrupted databases
questions.explanation: The aggregation pipeline processes documents through stages (like $match, $group, $sort, $project) to compute aggregated results.

questions.question: Which indexing feature ensures that no two documents have identical values for a specified field?
questions.explanation: A unique index ({ email: 1 }, { unique: true }) prevents duplicate values from being inserted.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Python List and a Tuple?
options: Lists are immutable; Tuples are mutable
Lists are mutable; Tuples are immutable
questions.explanation: Lists can be modified (mutable) after creation, whereas Tuples cannot be changed (immutable).

questions.question: What does the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in CPython do?
options: Restricts execution of Python bytecode to one native thread at a time
Compiles Python directly to machine code
questions.explanation: The GIL is a mutex that prevents multiple native threads from executing Python bytecodes simultaneously in CPython.

questions.question: Which built-in Python function returns both the index and value during loop iteration?
questions.explanation: enumerate(iterable) yields pairs containing an index count along with the value.

questions.question: What does a Python decorator do?
options: Adds graphic CSS styling to Python consoles
Wraps and alters or extends the behavior of a function or class without permanently modifying its source
questions.explanation: A decorator is a callable that accepts another function as an argument and extends its behavior.

questions.question: What is the output of: [x**2 for x in range(4) if x % 2 == 0]?
questions.explanation: The even numbers in range(4) are 0 and 2. Their squares are 0**2 = 0 and 2**2 = 4 -> [0, 4].

questions.question: If the speed of a train is 90 km/hr, what is its speed in meters per second (m/s)?
questions.explanation: Convert km/hr to m/s by multiplying by 5/18: 90 * (5/18) = 5 * 5 = 25 m/s.

questions.question: A product is bought for $400 and sold for $500. What is the profit percentage?
If 12 men can complete a project in 20 days, how many days will 15 men take to complete the same work?
questions.explanation: Total Work = 12 * 20 = 240 man-days. Days for 15 men = 240 / 15 = 16 days.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on $10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually.
The ratio of boys to girls in a class of 60 students is 3:2. How many girls are there in the class?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 3 + 2 = 5 parts. 1 part = 60 / 5 = 12. Girls = 2 * 12 = 24.

questions.question: Complete the numerical series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
Find the odd one out from the given group: Copper, Iron, Silver, Brass
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy (mixture of copper and zinc), whereas the others are pure elemental metals.

questions.question: In a certain code, TEACHER is written as VGCEJGT. How is CHILDREN written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted by +2 positions in the alphabet: C->E, H->J, I->K, L->N, D->F, R->T, E->G, N->P.

questions.question: Pointing to a man, a woman said: 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: 'Only daughter of my mother' refers to the woman herself. Therefore, she is the man's mother.

questions.question: A clock shows 4:30. If the minute hand points to the East, in which direction will the hour hand point?
questions.explanation: At 4:30, the minute hand is at 6 (South normally). If South is East (90 deg counter-clockwise), then between 4 and 5 (South-East normally) rotated 90 deg counter-clockwise points to North-East.

questions.question: Select the antonym for the word 'CANDID':
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward. Its antonym is 'Deceitful' or guarded.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Accommodate' with double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present in the auditorium.
questions.explanation: In 'Neither... nor...', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('the students' -> plural -> 'were').

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'To burn the midnight oil'?
options: To work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: 'To burn the midnight oil' means to work hard late at night.

questions.question: Convert to Passive Voice: 'The chef prepared a delicious dinner.'
options: A delicious dinner was prepared by the chef.
A delicious dinner is being prepared by the chef.
A delicious dinner had been prepared by the chef.
The dinner was preparing delicious by the chef.
questions.explanation: Simple past active ('prepared') becomes 'was prepared' in passive voice.

questions.question: Which artificial intelligence lab created the Transformer architecture in 2017 ('Attention Is All You Need')?
questions.explanation: The seminal Transformer paper 'Attention Is All You Need' was authored by Google Brain & Google Research researchers in 2017.

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars appears red due to the prevalence of iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

questions.question: Who is universally recognized as the pioneer of the World Wide Web (WWW)?
questions.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.question: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere by volume.

questions.question: What is the primary function of RAM in a computer system?
options: Fast volatile working memory for currently executing programs
questions.explanation: Random Access Memory (RAM) provides high-speed temporary read/write storage for active processes.
